source: KSQAAC Spardha Yashassu NMMS Study Material 2022, MAT Chapter 33 "Venn Diagrams" (questions: PDF pages 93–95, solutions: PDF page 169). Pictures cropped with tools/figures/ch33.json. tools/check_venn_diagrams.ts types in how the circles of every picture sit (inside, overlapping or apart) and how the groups in each question are related, and checks that exactly one option matches; all 15 agree with the key. Q2’s English says “Oviparous” and its Kannada ಜರಾಯುಜ (viviparous); either way the answer is B.

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows the relation between: Herbivorous, Carnivorous, Dog?
questions.rule: Some animals eat both plants and meat, so the two circles overlap. A dog eats both, so it goes where they overlap.
questions.working: Herbivorous and Carnivorous overlap; Dog is inside both.
questions.note: Strictly, a herbivore eats only plants and a carnivore only meat; the book counts a dog, which eats both, as in both groups.

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows the relation between: Oviparous animals, Bat, Lizard?
questions.rule: Oviparous animals lay eggs. A lizard lays eggs, so it is inside that circle; a bat gives birth to live young, so it is outside. Bats and lizards have nothing in common.
questions.working: One circle inside the big circle, and one circle outside it.
questions.note: The book’s Kannada says ಜರಾಯುಜ (animals that give birth to live young), and its key puts Bat inside that circle. Read either way, the answer is B: one group inside the big circle and one outside.

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows the relation between: Graduate, Professor, Singer?
questions.rule: Every professor is a graduate, so Professor is inside Graduate. Some graduates and some professors are singers, so Singer overlaps both.
questions.working: Professor inside Graduate; Singer overlaps both.

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows the relation between: Solar System, Comet, Galaxy?
questions.rule: A comet is part of the solar system, and the solar system is part of a galaxy: three circles, one inside the next.
questions.working: Comet inside Solar System inside Galaxy.

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows the relation between: Living Organisms, Mammals, Dog, Pigeon?
questions.rule: Mammals are living organisms, and a dog is a mammal. A pigeon is a living organism but not a mammal, so it is inside the big circle but outside Mammals.
questions.working: Dog inside Mammals inside Living Organisms; Pigeon inside Living Organisms only.

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows the relation between: Zero, Integers, Natural Numbers, Irrational Numbers?
questions.rule: Zero and the natural numbers are integers, and zero is not a natural number: two circles apart, inside Integers. No integer is irrational, so Irrational Numbers is a circle outside.
questions.working: Zero and Natural Numbers apart, both inside Integers; Irrational Numbers outside.

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows the relation between: Rhombus, Rectangle, Square, Parallelogram?
questions.rule: Rhombuses and rectangles are parallelograms, and a square is both a rhombus and a rectangle: Rhombus and Rectangle overlap inside Parallelogram, with Square where they overlap.
questions.working: Square inside Rhombus and Rectangle, which overlap inside Parallelogram.

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows the relation between: Nobel prize winners, Scientists, C.V. Raman?
questions.rule: Some scientists have won the Nobel prize, so the two circles overlap. C.V. Raman is a scientist who won it, so he is where they overlap.
questions.working: Nobel prize winners and Scientists overlap; C.V. Raman is inside both.

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows the relation between: Even Numbers, Prime Numbers, Natural Numbers?
questions.rule: Even numbers and prime numbers are natural numbers, and 2 is both even and prime: Even and Prime overlap inside Natural Numbers.
questions.working: Even and Prime overlap (at 2), both inside Natural Numbers.

questions.prompt: In a survey of 100 students, the students who drink coffee and tea are shown in the Venn diagram. How many students drink coffee?
questions.rule: Add every number inside the Coffee circle, including the part it shares with Tea.

questions.prompt: In a survey of 100 students, the students who drink coffee and tea are shown in the Venn diagram. How many students drink only tea?
questions.rule: Only tea: the part of the Tea circle outside the Coffee circle.

questions.prompt: In a survey of 100 students, the students who drink coffee and tea are shown in the Venn diagram. How many students drink both coffee and tea?
questions.rule: Both: the part where the two circles overlap.

questions.prompt: Which of these does the Venn diagram show?
questions.rule: Two groups overlap, and something is inside both. Some wild animals eat only plants, and an elephant is a wild animal that eats plants.
questions.working: Wild Animals and Herbivorous overlap; Elephant is inside both. A tiger is not herbivorous.

questions.prompt: Which of these does the Venn diagram show?
questions.rule: Two circles apart, both inside a big circle: two things with nothing in common, both part of one thing. The stick and the ball are both part of hockey.
questions.working: Stick and Ball apart, both inside Hockey.
questions.note: Players, Hockey, Kabaddi looks close, but some people play both hockey and kabaddi, so those two circles would overlap.

questions.prompt: Which of these does the Venn diagram show?
questions.rule: Three circles, each overlapping the other two, and all three meet: three groups where a person can be in any one, any two or all three. A teacher can also be a farmer and an actor.
questions.working: Teachers, Farmers and Actors all overlap. (Farmers and Teachers are inside Human beings, and a blackboard is not a person.)
questions.note: The book prints “Formers”; it means Farmers.
